Container.Name: ShadowPKG_exp
Container.Overview: A second ShadowPKG that runs alongside a stable one, for trying a build without risking the install you rely on. Everything that would collide is already separate here: its own image tag, container name, port and config folder. Build it under its own tag from the branch you want to try: docker build -t shadowpkg_exp:latest . — building it as shadowpkg:latest instead would replace the image your stable container picks up the next time it is recreated.
Container.Description: The same app as shadowpkg.xml, set up to sit beside an existing install rather than replace it. It differs only in the four things that would otherwise clash: the image tag it runs, the container name, the port, and the config folder holding profiles.json and the indexes. Both instances can read the same library; neither knows about the other.

Config.Name: WebUI Port
Config.Description: Host port for the web page and for the links handed to the console. 12801 rather than 12867 so it does not clash with a stable install. The container still listens on 12801 inside, which is why the container port here stays 12801.

Config.Name: Library
Config.Description: Main folder of .pkg files, e.g. /mnt/user/Games. Safe to point at the same folder as your stable install. Read/write is needed to unpack compressed archives from the app, and to rename or delete packages; read-only is fine for just browsing and sending, and is worth considering for a build you are still testing.

Config.Name: Extra Library
Config.Description: Optional. One more library, on top of the main one. Set the host path to the folder you want, and change the last part of the container path to whatever the library should be called — /extra-libraries/Retro shows up as a library named Retro. Add another entry the same way for each extra library.

Config.Name: Config
Config.Description: Holds profiles.json, settings.json, installed themes and the indexes. Must NOT be the folder your stable install uses: two versions sharing one archives.json and packages.json will overwrite each other's caches, and a console list edited in one would be changed under the other.

Config.Name: This server's address (PUBLIC_BASE)
Config.Description: Where the CONSOLE reaches THIS server: the IP of the machine running it plus THIS container's port, e.g. http://192.168.1.10:12801. Getting the port wrong here hands the console links to the other instance. Leave empty to work it out from the address you open the web page with, which is correct as long as you browse to this instance's port.

Config.Name: Name shown in the app (APP_NAME)
Config.Description: What this instance calls itself in the tab title, the Setup panel, the support report and the startup line, so two of them open side by side are not mistaken for one another. A send cannot be recalled, so this is worth setting. It changes nothing else.

Config.Name: PS5 address (PS5_HOST)
Config.Description: Optional. The CONSOLE's address, where its DPI v2 installer page is served, e.g. 192.168.1.50:12800 — the port is the payload's, not this container's. Only used to seed the first console on a fresh install; consoles are added and edited in the app itself.

Config.Name: ROOT_LABEL
Config.Description: Name shown for the main library. Changing it changes the links the app hands out, so avoid changing it while a console is downloading. Keep it the same as your stable install if you want the same links from both.

Config.Name: ALLOW_ANY_FILE
Config.Description: Set to 1 to browse and serve every file, not just .pkg. Off by default.

Config.Name: Follow a console that moved (FOLLOW_MOVES)
Config.Description: Optional. On by default: when a console stops answering, or an unknown address starts downloading from it, ShadowPKG looks for it on the local network and updates its saved address if there is exactly one console it could be. Set to 0 to turn that off; the console then just shows as not answering.

Config.Name: Log every range request (LOG_RANGES)
Config.Description: Optional. Set to 1 to log a start and a done line for every 16 MiB range request. By default a transfer is logged once when it starts, once when it completes, and whenever a range is cut short, so one big send does not push everything else out of the log.

Config.Name: Low space warning in GB (LOW_SPACE_GB)
Config.Description: A library with less than this many GB free gets a quiet warning in the Setup panel. 0 turns it off. Only a guide: on Unraid /mnt/user reports the pooled share, not the one disk a file will land on.

Config.Name: Notify when a build ends (NOTIFY_URL)
Config.Description: Optional. A URL that accepts a POST, called when a build finishes or fails (and, with NOTIFY_ON, when a download finishes or goes quiet): https://ntfy.sh/your-topic, a Discord or Slack webhook, or a Telegram sendMessage URL. Treat it as a secret.

Config.Name: What to notify about (NOTIFY_ON)
Config.Description: Only used with NOTIFY_URL. A comma separated list that replaces the default (builds): builds, downloads (a long download has finished, or gone quiet part way), problems (only the gone-quiet message), or all. Example: builds,downloads

Config.Name: Password for the page (ACCESS_PASSWORD)
Config.Description: Optional. Ask for this password (HTTP Basic) before showing the page or answering the API. Package links and the health check stay open, because a console cannot send a password. Sent unencrypted over plain HTTP, so it keeps out the curious, not someone watching the network.

Config.Name: User name (ACCESS_USER)
Config.Description: The user name that goes with the password above. Leave empty for shadow.

Config.Name: Allowed sites (ALLOWED_ORIGINS)
Config.Description: Optional, comma-separated. Extra sites a browser may post from, as https://pkg.example.com or just pkg.example.com. Only needed behind a reverse proxy that changes the Host header when the server address above is not the public one. Posts from any other site are refused.

Config.Name: Listen on one address (BIND_ADDRESS)
Config.Description: Optional. Listen on this one address instead of all. Leave it EMPTY on the default bridge network: an address the host has is not one this container has, and 127.0.0.1 would make the app unreachable. To limit it to one address there, publish the port to that address instead (Extra Parameters or the port mapping). Only useful with a host or custom network.

Config.Name: Theme for devices that have not chosen one (DEFAULT_THEME)
Config.Description: Optional. The look a phone, tablet or PC uses until it picks its own in the Theme window: ps1, ps1v2, midnight, purple, snes, dreamcast, wii, itsmemario, oled, nathan, win95, or the id of a theme you installed. A choice made in the Theme window (Every device without its own choice uses) takes priority. Leave empty for PS1.
